reader.requirement: At --std 85, the OCCURS DEPENDING ON data-name-1 and each ASCENDING/DESCENDING KEY data-name-2 may be written qualified (IN or OF, one or more levels, per §1985:IV.4.3.8.1), and the qualified name must bind to the one item the qualifiers select; since 1985 has no implicit qualification by the subject's groups, a name not unique in the program must be qualified.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.DialectLevel >= 2002: from 2002 the groups above the subject act as implicit qualifiers of DEPENDING ON and KEY names; below 2002 the whole scope's candidates are counted, so a non-unique unqualified name is ambiguous
SumCounterOperand85: at 1985 a report sum counter may be data-name-1 (kb/Work PB5310); not reached by these probes
takes the dialect level for the key item's own faults (another SR of 5.8.3), not the qualification

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: an unqualified DEPENDING ON or KEY name that is unique within the subject's group but declared elsewhere too is refused at 1985 (COBOL1639) and accepted at 2023 by implicit qualification; explicit qualification behaves the same at both
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf10_04 covers one-level OF qualification of both data-names; not exercised: two-level and IN qualification, a qualifier that selects nothing, the 1985 ambiguity of an unqualified name the 2002 rule would qualify implicitly

probes.expected: DEPENDING ON CNT IN G1 OF R1 (value 4, not R1's G2 CNT or R2's), DESCENDING KEY IS KY OF SUB IN ENT VL IN ENT, and 1985's optional ON/TIMES in DEPENDING CNT OF G2 all bind to the selected items; SEARCH ALL finds B=2; receiving T2 holds 2 occurrences

probes.printed: error COBOL1639: OCCURS DEPENDING ON data-name-1 of 'ENT' 'CNT' does not uniquely identify a data item - 2 declarations match
probes.expected: refused: a non-unique name must be qualified (§1985:IV.4.3.8.1 rule 1)

probes.printed: error COBOL0851: OCCURS DEPENDING ON 'CNT OF R2' on 'ENT': data-name-1 is not defined under the given qualifiers; error COBOL2353: OCCURS ASCENDING KEY IS 'KY OF OTHER-G' on 'ENT': no data item so named under the written qualifiers is 'ENT' itself or subordinate to it
probes.expected: refused: qualifiers selecting no item, and a qualified key outside the table (SR3)

probes.printed: error COBOL2024: OCCURS KEY IS 'KY OF ENT (1)' is written with a subscript
--std 85: two COBOL1639 (DEPENDING ON CNT and KEY IS KY each ambiguous); --std 2023: exit 0
probes.expected: 1985 has no implicit qualification, so both unqualified names must be qualified; 2023 qualifies them implicitly

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR2  (5.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2

reader.notes: Both operands go through ClauseDataName, which keeps the qualifier chain, and are resolved by counted candidate sets; the 1985 arm (no implicit qualifiers) is a distinct, correct arm. An early probe named an item OTHER, which is reserved at 1985 (COBOL0901); the rerun c4bad2b renames it.

refuter.evidence: Probes: r4fd --std 85 (sequential FD record: DEPENDING ON CNT IN F1, qualified by file-name per §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 format 1, while WS also declares CNT and KY; ASCENDING KEY IS KY OF REC1) writes and reads back the variable record, prints '3 [3ABC]' and SEARCH ALL 'FOUND B AT 3'. r4amb: DEPENDING ON CNT OF G1 where G1/CNT exist in R1 (the table's record) and in R2: --std 85 refused COBOL1639 '2 declarations match' (correct: 1985 has only explicit qualification), --std 2023 exit 0 '[AB]' (implicit qualification) -- the 1985 arm is distinct and correct for partial qualification too. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR2  (5.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2'; 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.1  (4.3.8.1 Qualification)  the text is in the clause; it lies in SRL2.1'.
